t.E927b.agn: In 1993 JECFA found its use in chewing gum as a texturiser and as a yeast nutrient acceptable.
t.E927b.body: Urea distributes readily into body fluids and is excreted mainly in urine: in pigs, 52% of labelled urea given in feed was excreted in urine and 1.3% in faeces within 48 hours.
t.E927b.found.0: Chewing gum without added sugar (max. 30,000 mg/kg)
t.E927b.prod: Produced chemically from carbon dioxide and ammonia or by hydrolysis of cyanamide.
t.E927b.regx.0: Use as a texturiser in chewing gum is acceptable.
t.E927b.regx.1: Only in chewing gum without added sugar, max. 30,000 mg/kg.
t.E927b.summary: A compound also known as urea. Used in chewing gum.
t.E927b.what: Carbamide (urea); used as a texturiser in chewing gum without added sugar.
